missing_requirements.title: Dual-Bank Buffer Alternating Concurrency Guard
missing_requirements.description: The flight data recorder buffer must implement a dual-bank (ping-pong) or atomic ring-buffer architecture with explicit memory barrier synchronization to prevent race conditions and data corruption between the continuous ARINC 429 high-rate frame ingestion writer thread and the emergency power-loss flash memory serialization reader.
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: Continuous ARINC 429 bus frame ingestion concurrently writes into volatile memory while an emergency power-loss event triggers an immediate read and flush operation. Step 2: Without strict concurrency isolation or dual-bank locking, simultaneous read-write access to the active buffer pointer will cause memory tearing, pointer corruption, and partial frame loss. Step 3: Therefore, a deterministic dual-bank memory switching invariant with hardware memory barriers is strictly required to guarantee zero data loss and bit-exact preservation during the transition.

missing_requirements.title: Flight Recorder Data Integrity Checksum and Framing Verification
missing_requirements.description: The system shall append cryptographic or cyclic redundancy check (CRC-32/ARINC) markers to every flushed block of ARINC 429 frames before committing to the solid-state crash-survivable memory to validate data integrity upon post-crash retrieval and readout analysis.
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: Crash-survivable memory units undergo extreme physical trauma, intense deceleration forces, and post-impact thermal exposure which can induce bit-flips or corruption in stored flash cells. Step 2: Merely dumping raw buffer bytes without validation metadata prevents investigators from verifying whether recovered frames are authentic or bit-corrupted. Step 3: Therefore, computing and embedding robust CRC checksums per data block is a mandatory aerospace engineering safety requirement for verifiable accident reconstruction.

missing_requirements.title: Emergency Flash Write Failure Recovery and Byte Retry Mechanism
missing_requirements.description: If a write or block erasure error occurs on the solid-state crash-survivable memory during the emergency power-loss flush sequence, the system must immediately attempt sector re-mapping or fallback retry sequences within the remaining hold-up power duration.
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: Non-volatile solid-state memory sectors can experience localized wear-out or transient hardware faults during high-g impact or sudden power failure transients. Step 2: A single unhandled write exception or hardware timeout during the emergency flush window would abort data persistence and result in catastrophic loss of flight recorder telemetry. Step 3: Therefore, an explicit fault-tolerant retry and sector-fallback protocol must be executed within the bounded hold-up window to ensure maximum survivability of critical flight parameters.
